intent.raw_query: Maldives honeymoon for 2, $5000 budget, snorkeling and luxury resorts, March 2026

experiences.name: Private Lagoon Snorkeling at House Reef
experiences.description: Snorkel directly from your overwater bungalow at a resort with an accessible house reef. Ideal for honeymooners seeking intimate underwater exploration without boat transfers. Look for resorts in North Malé Atoll such as those near Veligandu or Kuredu where the house reef is steps away, maximizing your 13-day stay from Day 1 arrival evening onward.

experiences.name: Sunset Dolphin Cruise for Two
experiences.description: Board a private dhoni (traditional Maldivian boat) for a romantic sunset cruise to spot spinner dolphins in their natural habitat. Many resorts in South Malé Atoll offer this as an in-resort excursion, keeping travel time minimal. Champagne and canapés included for a honeymoon-perfect experience.

experiences.name: Underwater Restaurant Dining Experience
experiences.description: Enjoy a candlelit dinner surrounded by coral reefs and marine life at an underwater restaurant. Ithaa Undersea Restaurant at Conrad Maldives Rangali Island or similar venues in Ari Atoll offer world-class Maldivian and international cuisine. Book well in advance; this is a bucket-list romantic dining experience perfect for honeymooners.

experiences.name: Manta Ray Snorkeling at Hanifaru Bay
experiences.description: Snorkel alongside majestic manta rays at UNESCO Biosphere Reserve Hanifaru Bay, one of the world's best manta ray aggregation sites. Best experienced May through November. Choose a resort in Baa Atoll to minimize transfer time and maximize water time. A guided group snorkel keeps costs low while delivering a luxury-level natural spectacle.

experiences.name: Maldivian Cultural Village Tour on Maafushi Island
experiences.description: Take a short speedboat trip to the local inhabited island of Maafushi to explore traditional Maldivian culture, visit a local mosque, taste authentic Maldivian street food like mas huni and hedhikaa, and browse handcrafted lacquerware. A meaningful cultural contrast to resort luxury, offering authentic connection to Maldivian heritage without straying far from South Malé Atoll resort hubs.
experiences.location: Maafushi Island, South Malé Atoll, Maldives

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Maldives
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Private Lagoon Snorkeling at House Reef
experiences.description: Snorkel directly from your overwater bungalow at a resort with an accessible house reef. Ideal for honeymooners seeking intimate underwater exploration without boat transfers. Look for resorts in North Malé Atoll such as those near Veligandu or Kuredu where the house reef is steps away, maximizing your 13-day stay from Day 1 arrival evening onward.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and collect luggage. Take a budget-friendly public ferry or shared speedboat transfer to North Malé Atoll. Check in to the North Malé Atoll Boutique Stay. Freshen up, unpack, and explore the guesthouse surroundings. Take a leisurely stroll along the local island beach and get oriented with the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Watch your first Maldivian sunset from the beach near the guesthouse. Enjoy a relaxed welcome evening — sit by the shore, listen to the waves, and soak in the atmosphere of arriving in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during transit — grab a snack from the airport café or bring your own
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a small local café near the ferry terminal in Malé (rice and curry from a local eatery, approx. $3–5)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local island restaurant near the guesthouse — try fresh grilled fish with rice and salad (approx. $8–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry transfer in advance to save money vs. private speedboat. Public ferries cost around $1–3 USD. Keep some USD cash handy as many local island shops and eateries prefer cash. The guesthouse may offer a welcome drink — enjoy it!

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and enjoy a sunrise walk on the beach. After breakfast, head to the guesthouse's house reef for your first snorkeling session. Explore the vibrant coral gardens and spot tropical fish, rays, and possibly sea turtles. Rent snorkel gear from the guesthouse if you don't have your own (approx. $5–8/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget group snorkeling excursion organized by the guesthouse to a nearby snorkeling hotspot in North Malé Atoll — often includes 2–3 snorkel spots, a sandbank visit, and dolphin watching (approx. $30–45 per person). Enjoy the stunning turquoise waters and diverse marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the guesthouse and rinse off. Take a romantic evening walk along the beach as the sun sets. Sit together on the shore and stargaze — the Maldives offers incredible dark skies away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the guesthouse — typically included or available for $4–7 (eggs, toast, fresh fruit, tea/coffee)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the snorkeling boat or a quick local meal at a beachside café (tuna sandwich or short eats, approx. $4–6)
meals.dinner: Romantic candlelit dinner for two at a local island restaurant — fresh seafood platter with grilled fish, salad, and coconut rice (approx. $15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — regular sunscreen damages coral reefs and is banned in many Maldivian resorts. Bring a reusable water bottle. The group snorkeling excursion is the most budget-friendly way to see multiple sites in one day.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling session at the house reef — go early when the water is calmest and visibility is best. Look for nurse sharks resting on the sandy bottom and colorful parrotfish. Spend 1–2 hours exploring at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local inhabited island by public ferry (very affordable, often $1–2 per trip). Walk through the island village, observe traditional Maldivian life, visit the local market, and browse handmade crafts and souvenirs. This offers an authentic cultural experience rarely seen by resort-only tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the guesthouse before sunset. Enjoy a couple's massage or spa treatment if the guesthouse offers one (local guesthouses often offer affordable massages at $30–50 for 60 minutes). Relax on the beach with a mocktail or fresh coconut.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — fresh tropical fruit, yogurt, and local flatbread (roshi) with tuna paste (mas huni)
meals.lunch: Eat at a local tea shop (sai hotel) on the inhabited island — short eats like bajiya (tuna pastry) and samosas with tea (approx. $3–5)
meals.dinner: Barbecue night at the guesthouse beach if available, or local restaurant with grilled lobster or barracuda (approx. $12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting local inhabited islands — shoulders and knees should be covered out of respect for the Muslim community. Bikinis are only appropriate on designated bikini beaches. Carry a light scarf or sarong.

day_by_day.morning: Book a budget manta ray or whale shark snorkeling excursion — North Malé Atoll is famous for seasonal manta ray sightings. Check with your guesthouse for the best current spots. Group tours run approximately $50–70 per person and are absolutely worth the splurge for a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning excursion, relax on a stunning sandbank (sandbank picnic tours available through guesthouse for approx. $20–30 per person). Spend the afternoon lounging on a pristine white sandbar surrounded by crystal-clear water — a quintessential Maldives experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset fishing trip — a traditional Maldivian experience where you fish by hand line from a dhoni (local wooden boat). Many guesthouses offer this for $20–30 per person. Your catch may be cooked for dinner!

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the morning excursion — toast, eggs, and fresh juice at the guesthouse
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the sandbank or boat — sandwiches, fresh fruit, and water provided by the tour operator
meals.dinner: Your freshly caught fish grilled at the guesthouse or a local restaurant — a truly romantic and memorable meal (cooking fee approx. $5–8 if you bring your own catch)

day_by_day.notes: Manta ray and whale shark sightings depend on season and luck — March is generally a good month in North Malé Atoll. Always maintain a respectful distance from marine life. Never touch or chase mantas or whale sharks.

day_by_day.morning: Lazy morning — sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. This is your rest and recharge day. Spend the morning reading, journaling, or simply floating in the lagoon near the guesthouse. Take photos of the incredible turquoise water and capture memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the capital city Malé by public ferry (approx. $1 each way from North Malé Atoll). Explore the colorful fish market, visit the Grand Friday Mosque (Masjid al-Sultan Muhammad Thakurufaanu Al Auzam), browse the local market for souvenirs, and walk through the vibrant streets of this compact island capital.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Malé's waterfront promenade at dusk. Watch local fishermen return with their catch. Take the public ferry back to your island. Enjoy a quiet romantic evening at the guesthouse beach.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent guesthouse breakfast — pancakes with fresh tropical fruit and coconut syrup, or a full cooked breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch in Malé at a local restaurant — try garudhiya (tuna broth soup) with rice and lime, or a full Maldivian rice and curry spread (approx. $4–7)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachside restaurant near the guesthouse — fresh tuna steak or octopus curry with coconut rice (approx. $10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Friday is the holy day in the Maldives — the Grand Friday Mosque is most active during Friday prayers (around 12:00 noon). Non-Muslims cannot enter during prayer time. The fish market is most lively in the early morning. Malé is very walkable — the entire island can be crossed on foot in 20 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkeling at the house reef during high tide for the best visibility and marine life activity. Focus on finding sea turtles — they are commonly spotted in North Malé Atoll reefs in the morning. Spend 2 hours exploring different sections of the reef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day diving or snorkeling trip to a famous dive site in North Malé Atoll such as Banana Reef or HP Reef (also known as Rainbow Reef) — considered among the best dive sites in the world. Non-divers can snorkel at the surface while divers explore the depths (group trip approx. $35–55 for snorkelers).
day_by_day.evening: Romantic beach picnic — ask your guesthouse to prepare a simple picnic basket with local snacks, fresh fruit, and drinks. Spread a blanket on the beach, watch the stars emerge, and enjoy a private moment together as the warm Maldivian night envelops you.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-snorkeling breakfast — fresh fruit, yogurt, and granola at the guesthouse
meals.lunch: On the boat or at a local café after the excursion — grilled fish wrap or tuna salad (approx. $5–8)
meals.dinner: Romantic beach picnic with guesthouse-prepared local snacks, fresh tropical fruit, coconut water, and local sweets (approx. $15–20 for two)

day_by_day.notes: Banana Reef is one of the Maldives' most iconic dive sites — the snorkeling from the surface is also spectacular with excellent visibility. Book the excursion the day before to secure spots. Bring an underwater camera or rent a GoPro from the guesthouse if available.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip relaxation day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Spend the morning doing absolutely nothing — this is the Maldives, and sometimes the best activity is simply floating in the warm Indian Ocean and listening to the sound of the waves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local island on foot or by bicycle (rent from guesthouse for approx. $5–8/day). Visit the local school, community center, and small shops. Chat with friendly locals and learn about island life. Visit the local lagoon for a swim in calm, shallow waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dhoni cruise — book a romantic shared sunset cruise on a traditional Maldivian wooden boat (approx. $25–35 per person). Watch the sky turn shades of orange, pink, and purple over the Indian Ocean while sipping fresh coconut water.

meals.breakfast: Full guesthouse breakfast — enjoy a slow, indulgent meal with everything on the menu
meals.lunch: Cook your own simple meal if the guesthouse has a guest kitchen, or grab fresh fruit and snacks from the local shop (budget: $3–5)
meals.dinner: Special mid-trip dinner at the best local restaurant on the island — splurge slightly on a seafood feast with lobster, grilled fish, and coconut dessert (approx. $20–25 per person as a treat)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 marks the halfway point of your trip — a perfect time to rest, reflect, and recharge. Don't feel guilty about doing nothing — relaxation is a key part of the Maldives experience. Check your snorkel gear for any needed repairs or replacements.

day_by_day.morning: Join a private lagoon snorkeling session at a resort with an accessible house reef — the 'Private Lagoon Snorkeling at House Reef' experience. Snorkel directly from an overwater bungalow area at a nearby resort that offers day passes (approx. $50–80 per person for a resort day pass, which often includes lunch and use of facilities). This is your luxury splurge day!
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying the resort day pass — use the infinity pool, relax on the overwater deck, enjoy the pristine resort beach, and soak in the luxury atmosphere. Take photos on the iconic overwater bungalow jetty for stunning memories.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your guesthouse feeling refreshed and having experienced a taste of Maldivian luxury. Enjoy a quiet, romantic evening on your guesthouse beach, reminiscing about the day's highlights.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the guesthouse before heading to the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch included in the resort day pass — enjoy the resort restaurant's buffet or à la carte menu (included in day pass cost)
meals.dinner: Back at the guesthouse — simple, budget-friendly local meal to balance the day's splurge (local fish curry and rice, approx. $8–10 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Research resort day passes in advance — some resorts in North Malé Atoll offer day passes that include meals, snorkeling equipment, and use of water sports facilities. This is the most budget-friendly way to experience overwater bungalow luxury without paying for accommodation. Book at least 2–3 days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bioluminescent beach walk — if conditions are right (check with guesthouse), walk the beach after dark to spot glowing plankton in the waves. Alternatively, go for a pre-sunrise snorkel at the house reef when nocturnal marine life is still active and the reef is peaceful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full-day island hopping excursion covering 3–4 islands in North Malé Atoll — typically includes a local village island, a resort island viewpoint, a sandbank, and a snorkeling spot (group tours approx. $40–60 per person). A great way to see the variety the atoll has to offer.
day_by_day.evening: Return from island hopping and enjoy a relaxing evening. Try a DIY romantic setup — ask the guesthouse to arrange simple flower petals and candles in your room as a surprise (many budget guesthouses offer this for a small fee of $10–20).

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the guesthouse — fruit, cereal, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the island hopping dhoni or a meal at a local island tea shop during the tour
meals.dinner: Romantic dinner at the guesthouse's beach area if they offer outdoor dining, or nearby restaurant — try Maldivian lobster if budget allows (approx. $15–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bioluminescent plankton (sea sparkle) is most visible on dark, moonless nights from June to February, but can occasionally be spotted in March. Ask locals for current conditions. The island hopping tour is excellent for photography — bring a fully charged camera and extra memory cards.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or meditation on the beach — many guesthouses offer free or low-cost yoga sessions at sunrise (approx. $5–10 if charged). Start the day with mindfulness and connect with the natural beauty surrounding you. Follow with a refreshing swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Underwater photography session — rent an underwater camera or GoPro and spend 2–3 hours documenting the incredible marine life at the house reef. Focus on coral formations, fish schools, and any turtles or rays you encounter. This creates lasting honeymoon memories.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the local island's bikini beach for a final afternoon swim, then watch the sunset together. In the evening, attend a local cultural show if available — traditional Maldivian bodu beru drumming performances are sometimes organized for tourists (check with guesthouse).

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga breakfast — smoothie bowl, fresh tropical fruits, and coconut water at the guesthouse
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the guesthouse or local café — tuna salad, fresh bread, and iced tea (approx. $6–9)
meals.dinner: Try cooking a Maldivian meal yourself if the guesthouse has a kitchen — buy fresh fish from the local market and prepare a simple curry, or enjoy a full local dinner at a restaurant (approx. $10–14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Many budget guesthouses in the Maldives have guest kitchens — cooking your own meals even once or twice during the trip can significantly reduce food costs. Local markets sell fresh fish, vegetables, and spices at very affordable prices. This is also a fun cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final major snorkeling adventure — book a specialized snorkeling trip to a shark point or turtle cleaning station in North Malé Atoll. These sites are known for frequent sightings of blacktip reef sharks, white tip sharks, green sea turtles, and eagle rays (group tour approx. $35–50 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return and spend the afternoon souvenir shopping at the local island market. Look for handmade lacquerware, woven palm leaf crafts, local spices, and Maldivian sarongs (feyli). Budget $20–50 for souvenirs. Pack carefully to protect fragile items.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-to-the-sea swim at sunset — wade into the warm water one last time before your final days. Watch the sun sink below the horizon and take in the beauty of the Maldives at its most magical hour. Write postcards or journal entries to capture your memories.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — full spread to fuel the morning snorkeling adventure
meals.lunch: On the boat or at a local eatery after the excursion — fresh fish and chips or a local rice and curry plate (approx. $5–8)
meals.dinner: Penultimate dinner at your favorite local restaurant discovered during the trip — order your favorite dish from the past 11 days (approx. $10–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start consolidating your packing today to avoid a stressful last morning. Check if the guesthouse offers a luggage storage service for your last day. Confirm your ferry/speedboat transfer timing back to the airport for your departure day. Tip your guesthouse staff if you've had excellent service.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise snorkel at the house reef — wake up early for one last magical underwater experience. Say goodbye to the fish, corals, and sea turtles that have accompanied you throughout the trip. Spend 1–1.5 hours savoring every moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the guesthouse (or arrange a late checkout if available for a small fee). Store luggage at the guesthouse and spend your last free hours on the beach. Swim, sunbathe, and take final photos. Write a heartfelt review for your guesthouse to help other budget travelers.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner on the island — choose the most romantic spot you've discovered during your stay. Dress up slightly and make it a special occasion. Toast to your honeymoon, to the Maldives, and to each other with fresh coconut or a mocktail.

meals.breakfast: Final guesthouse breakfast — savor every bite knowing it's your last morning here
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café or guesthouse — keep it simple and affordable (approx. $5–8)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner — splurge on a romantic seafood dinner with the best view available (approx. $20–30 per person as a final treat)

day_by_day.notes: If your flight departs on Day 13, confirm the exact ferry/speedboat transfer time needed to reach the airport comfortably. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for transfers, check-in, and security. Keep essential items and valuables in your carry-on.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Maldives. Wake up early for one last beach walk and sunrise. Take final photos and videos of the paradise you've called home for nearly two weeks. Pack any remaining items and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the public ferry or arranged transfer back to Malé and then to Velana International Airport. Arrive at the airport with plenty of time. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts — Maldivian honey, local chocolates, or reef-safe sunscreen make great souvenirs. Board your flight home with hearts full of incredible memories.
day_by_day.evening: In transit — reflect on your 13-day Maldives honeymoon adventure. Review your photos, relive your favorite moments, and start planning your next adventure together.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the guesthouse or grab something from a local bakery before the ferry — keep it light for travel
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café — treat yourself to one last Maldivian meal if time allows before departure (approx. $8–15)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip summary for the trip: Public ferries saved significant money vs. speedboats. Eating at local tea shops and restaurants rather than resort restaurants kept food costs low. Group excursions vs. private tours halved activity costs. Total estimated budget for two people for 13 days (excluding flights): $1,200–1,800 USD covering accommodation, food, activities, and transfers. The Maldives on a budget is absolutely possible and equally magical!

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, then transfer via speedboat to your North Malé Atoll Boutique Stay (approx. 20–40 min). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the resort's private beach to get your bearings. Unpack and settle into your romantic retreat.
day_by_day.evening: Watch your first Maldivian sunset from the beach or your room's terrace with a welcome cocktail. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's main restaurant — opt for fresh grilled seafood and local Maldivian curry dishes.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at Velana Airport café before or after landing
meals.dinner: Resort main restaurant — fresh grilled fish, Maldivian curry rice, and tropical fruit platter (mid-range set menu, ~$40–60 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light and relaxing. Confirm speedboat transfer with the resort in advance. Ask the front desk about house reef snorkeling conditions and book any excursions for upcoming days.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast, head out for your first Private Lagoon Snorkeling at the House Reef session. Gear up at the resort's dive/snorkel center and explore the coral gardens and colorful marine life directly accessible from the overwater bungalow area. Ideal for couples — go at your own pace for 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort, rinse off, and spend the afternoon lounging by the infinity pool or on the beach. Enjoy a light poolside lunch. In the mid-afternoon, book a couples' spa treatment at the resort spa — try a traditional Maldivian coconut oil massage or a couples' scrub package.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll hand-in-hand along the beach at dusk. Dine at the resort's beachside grill for a romantic dinner under the stars with tiki torches and ocean sounds.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — tropical fruits, eggs, pastries, fresh juices
meals.lunch: Poolside light lunch — sandwiches, fresh coconut, tropical smoothies (~$15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Beachside grill at resort — grilled lobster or snapper, salad, and dessert (~$50–70 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the couples' spa session early in the morning to secure your preferred time slot. Check if the resort offers a complimentary snorkel gear package for guests.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise yoga session on the beach or deck (many boutique resorts offer complimentary morning yoga). Follow with a hearty breakfast before preparing for today's main excursion — the Maldivian Cultural Village Tour on Maafushi Island. Board a speedboat (~20–30 min ride) to the local inhabited island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Maafushi Island with a local guide. Visit the traditional fishing village, a local school, a mosque, and craft workshops. Shop for handmade souvenirs like lacquer work and woven mats. Try local street food at a small café — fresh tuna roshi (flatbread) and hedhikaa (local snacks). Return to the resort by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort after the cultural excursion. Enjoy a sundowner cocktail at the resort's overwater bar. Have dinner at the resort's à la carte restaurant featuring a fusion of Maldivian and Asian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — eggs, fresh tropical fruits, Maldivian mas huni (tuna and coconut) on request
meals.lunch: Local café on Maafushi Island — tuna roshi, hedhikaa snacks, fresh lime juice (~$8–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Resort à la carte restaurant — tuna tataki, prawn curry, mango sorbet (~$45–60 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting Maafushi (cover shoulders and knees as it is a local Muslim island). Carry some Maldivian Rufiyaa or USD for local purchases. The speedboat transfer is usually arranged by the resort (~$20–30 round trip).

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow morning with breakfast in bed or on your terrace — a romantic treat you can request from the resort. Spend the morning doing a second, more exploratory House Reef snorkeling session, this time venturing to the deeper edges of the reef to spot sea turtles, rays, and reef sharks if conditions allow.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, rent a kayak or paddleboard from the resort's water sports center and explore the calm lagoon waters together. Paddle to a nearby sandbank for a private picnic-style afternoon (ask the resort to prepare a small picnic basket in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Tonight, dress up for the Underwater Restaurant Dining Experience — one of the Maldives' most iconic romantic experiences. Dine surrounded by coral reefs and marine life in a breathtaking submerged setting. This requires a short boat transfer, so arrange transport with the resort.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast service — fresh juice, pastries, eggs, tropical fruits (small surcharge may apply)
meals.lunch: Resort casual café — grilled fish wrap, fresh salad, iced tea (~$20–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Underwater restaurant — 3-course set menu with wine pairing (~$120–180 per person, splurge-worthy special occasion dinner)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Underwater Restaurant Dining Experience well in advance as it fills up quickly, especially for couples. Confirm boat transfer logistics with the resort. The sandbank picnic should also be pre-arranged at least a day ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Today is a rest and rejuvenation day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Spend the morning reading by the pool or beach, or take an optional guided snorkeling tour organized by the resort to a nearby reef patch just a short boat ride away.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the resort's spa again for a longer couples' wellness package — try a 90-minute Ayurvedic or hot stone massage. Alternatively, take a cooking class at the resort (if offered) to learn how to make traditional Maldivian dishes like garudhiya (fish broth) and bis keemiya (stuffed pastries).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a casual dinner at the resort's casual dining venue or beach bar. Toast to your trip with a bottle of local fruit wine or imported wine and share a platter of fresh seafood tapas.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — full spread with Maldivian and international options
meals.lunch: Light poolside snacks — hummus platter, fresh fruit, sparkling water (~$12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Resort beach bar — seafood tapas platter, grilled corn, tropical cocktails (~$35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day to avoid over-scheduling. The Maldives is best enjoyed slowly. If the cooking class is available, book it the day before. Check the resort's weekly activity schedule for complimentary offerings.

day_by_day.morning: Set off early for the Sunset Dolphin Cruise for Two — book the morning departure if available, or the late afternoon slot (see evening). If morning, board a private traditional dhoni boat and head out into open waters to spot spinner dolphins leaping and playing in the bow wave. A magical, intimate experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the cruise and enjoy a relaxed beach afternoon. Try snorkeling one more time at the house reef, this time focusing on underwater photography — rent or bring an underwater camera. Spend time drying off in hammocks or sun loungers.
day_by_day.evening: If the dolphin cruise is an evening excursion, depart around 17:30 to catch the sunset on the water with dolphins. Return after dark with champagne on board. Afterward, have a quiet dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — light and energizing before the boat trip
meals.lunch: Resort restaurant — grilled chicken or fish with rice and salad (~$25–35 per person)
meals.dinner: Resort main restaurant or in-room dining — pasta, fresh fish, dessert (~$40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Sunset Dolphin Cruise is best timed for late afternoon (17:00–19:00) for the most romantic experience. Confirm with the tour operator whether champagne or refreshments are included. Bring a light jacket as it can get breezy on the open water.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint of the trip — celebrate with a special breakfast. Request a romantic beach breakfast setup from the resort (table on the sand, flowers, fresh juice, eggs made to order). Then spend the morning in a guided glass-bottom boat tour around the lagoon to observe coral and fish without getting wet — great for a relaxed morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to the resort and spend the afternoon exploring the resort's facilities you haven't tried yet — perhaps a game of beach volleyball, a visit to the resort boutique for souvenirs, or simply floating in the lagoon with snorkel masks.
day_by_day.evening: Tonight, arrange a private candlelit beach dinner — a classic Maldives honeymoon experience. Many boutique resorts offer this as a special package with a dedicated waiter, fairy lights, and a custom menu. Book at least 2 days in advance.

meals.breakfast: Private beach breakfast setup — fresh juices, eggs benedict, tropical fruits, croissants (~$30–40 surcharge for the setup)
meals.lunch: Resort café — tuna melt sandwich, coconut water, fresh salad (~$18–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Private candlelit beach dinner — 4-course set menu with wine (~$100–150 per person, special occasion experience)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a great milestone to celebrate your week in paradise. The private beach dinner must be pre-booked and may require a minimum spend. Check weather conditions in advance as outdoor dining can be affected by wind.

day_by_day.morning: Today is an adventure day. Join a guided big-game fishing excursion or a reef fishing trip organized by the resort. Spend 2–3 hours on a traditional dhoni trying your hand at Maldivian-style fishing. The catch may even be cooked for your lunch!
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by midday. If you caught fish, ask the kitchen to prepare it for lunch — a truly farm-to-table experience. Spend the afternoon at leisure, perhaps revisiting the house reef for a final snorkel or relaxing with a book in a hammock over the water.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Bodu Beru cultural performance if organized by the resort (traditional Maldivian drumming and dance, often held on weekend evenings). Dine at the resort restaurant afterward.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — energizing meal before the fishing trip
meals.lunch: Resort kitchen prepares your fresh catch — grilled fish with rice, salad, and coconut chutney (complimentary or small fee)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — Maldivian curry night special, roshi, and tropical dessert (~$40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The fishing excursion typically costs $50–80 per person and lasts 2–3 hours. Confirm with the resort if they will cook your catch. Bodu Beru performances are usually free for resort guests — check the weekly schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to a nearby uninhabited sandbank island — a quintessential Maldives experience. Arrange with the resort for a private or small-group speedboat transfer. Walk barefoot on powdery white sand surrounded by turquoise water with no one else around.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkel around the sandbank's edges to discover small reef fish and coral formations. Return to the resort by early afternoon. Spend the rest of the afternoon at the spa or pool.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort's overwater bar — sip cocktails while watching the stars emerge over the Indian Ocean. Opt for a lighter dinner at the beach bar or casual restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — light and fresh
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the sandbank arranged by the resort — sandwiches, fruit, water, and snacks (~$20–30 per person add-on)
meals.dinner: Resort beach bar — grilled calamari, fish tacos, tropical mocktails or cocktails (~$30–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The sandbank excursion is weather-dependent. Book it through the resort's excursion desk. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water as there is no shade on a sandbank.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the highlight excursion of the trip — Manta Ray Snorkeling at Hanifaru Bay in the Baa Atoll UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. This requires an early departure (around 7:00–8:00 AM) via speedboat (approximately 1.5–2 hours each way). Snorkel alongside dozens of manta rays feeding in the bay — a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return journey from Hanifaru Bay. Arrive back at the resort by mid-to-late afternoon. Rest and recover from the full-day excursion with a refreshing swim in the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourselves to a quiet, comfortable dinner at the resort after the long day. Share stories and photos from the manta ray encounter over a relaxed meal.

meals.breakfast: Early resort buffet or grab-and-go breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the boat provided by the tour operator — sandwiches, fruit, water (usually included in excursion price)
meals.dinner: Resort main restaurant — comfort food, pasta or grilled fish, dessert (~$40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanifaru Bay manta ray snorkeling is seasonal (best May–November, but rays can be present year-round). March is transitional — confirm sightings with the tour operator before booking. The excursion typically costs $100–150 per person including guide, gear, and lunch. Only snorkeling is permitted in Hanifaru Bay (no scuba diving).

day_by_day.morning: A gentle morning after yesterday's big adventure. Enjoy a slow breakfast and then take a final, unhurried snorkeling session at the house reef — say goodbye to the coral and fish you've come to recognize over the past days. Take your time and soak it all in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon shopping at the resort boutique for last-minute gifts and souvenirs — Maldivian lacquerwork, sarongs, and local spices make great keepsakes. Then enjoy a couples' pedicure or foot massage at the spa.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Underwater Restaurant or the resort's finest dining venue for a special penultimate evening dinner — a chance to relive the magic of earlier in the trip. Toast to an unforgettable honeymoon.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — enjoy your favorites one more time
meals.lunch: Casual poolside lunch — fresh salad bowl, grilled chicken, iced coffee (~$20–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — chef's tasting menu or à la carte, wine pairing (~$80–120 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to wrap up any unfinished experiences and begin packing non-essentials. Confirm checkout time and departure transfer arrangements with the front desk.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning in the Maldives. Wake up early to catch the sunrise over the Indian Ocean — one last magical moment together. Take photos from your terrace or the beach. Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort (standard checkout is usually 12:00 noon — request a late checkout if available). Spend remaining time at the pool or beach. If time allows, take one last short snorkel at the house reef before the transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer back to Velana International Airport via speedboat. Depending on your flight time, explore the airport's duty-free shops for Maldivian souvenirs, local chocolates, and gifts. Enjoy a final Maldivian meal at the airport restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Final resort buffet breakfast — indulge in all your favorites
meals.lunch: Light meal at the resort before checkout or at the airport — fish curry rice or a sandwich (~$15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or lounge — fresh seafood, Maldivian curry, tropical juice (~$25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm speedboat transfer timing based on your departure flight. Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for the boat transfer, check-in, and security. Keep a small amount of USD handy for tips and last-minute purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day — board your flight home carrying incredible memories of your Maldives honeymoon. If your flight departs in the afternoon or evening, enjoy the airport lounge or a final coffee overlooking the runway and turquoise waters of the atoll.
day_by_day.afternoon: In-flight — relax, watch movies, and reminisce about your favorite moments. Begin planning which Maldivian island you'll visit next!
day_by_day.evening: Arrive home refreshed, sun-kissed, and deeply connected after an unforgettable 13-day romantic escape in the Maldives.

meals.breakfast: Airport café or lounge breakfast — coffee, pastries, fresh juice
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or airport restaurant if there is a long layover
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel/departure day. Ensure all resort bills are settled before checkout on Day 12. Keep passports, boarding passes, and travel insurance documents easily accessible. Consider writing a review of your resort and experiences to help future travelers.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Maldives Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Private Lagoon Snorkeling at House Reef
experiences.description: Snorkel directly from your overwater bungalow at a resort with an accessible house reef. Ideal for honeymooners seeking intimate underwater exploration without boat transfers. Look for resorts in North Malé Atoll such as those near Veligandu or Kuredu where the house reef is steps away, maximizing your 13-day stay from Day 1 arrival evening onward.

experiences.name: Sunset Dolphin Cruise for Two
experiences.description: Board a private dhoni (traditional Maldivian boat) for a romantic sunset cruise to spot spinner dolphins in their natural habitat. Many resorts in South Malé Atoll offer this as an in-resort excursion, keeping travel time minimal. Champagne and canapés included for a honeymoon-perfect experience.

experiences.name: Underwater Restaurant Dining Experience
experiences.description: Enjoy a candlelit dinner surrounded by coral reefs and marine life at an underwater restaurant. Ithaa Undersea Restaurant at Conrad Maldives Rangali Island or similar venues in Ari Atoll offer world-class Maldivian and international cuisine. Book well in advance; this is a bucket-list romantic dining experience perfect for honeymooners.

experiences.name: Manta Ray Snorkeling at Hanifaru Bay
experiences.description: Snorkel alongside majestic manta rays at UNESCO Biosphere Reserve Hanifaru Bay, one of the world's best manta ray aggregation sites. Best experienced May through November. Choose a resort in Baa Atoll to minimize transfer time and maximize water time. A guided group snorkel keeps costs low while delivering a luxury-level natural spectacle.

experiences.name: Maldivian Cultural Village Tour on Maafushi Island
experiences.description: Take a short speedboat trip to the local inhabited island of Maafushi to explore traditional Maldivian culture, visit a local mosque, taste authentic Maldivian street food like mas huni and hedhikaa, and browse handcrafted lacquerware. A meaningful cultural contrast to resort luxury, offering authentic connection to Maldivian heritage without straying far from South Malé Atoll resort hubs.
experiences.location: Maafushi Island, South Malé Atoll, Maldives

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Met by a private resort representative for a seamless VIP transfer via luxury speedboat to North Malé Atoll Boutique Stay. Check-in with a welcome ceremony featuring fresh coconut water and traditional flower garlands. Settle into your overwater bungalow and enjoy a private villa orientation. Take a leisurely stroll along the jetty and soak in your first views of the turquoise lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a romantic welcome sunset cocktail on your private deck as the sun dips below the horizon. Freshen up and head to the resort's signature overwater restaurant for an intimate candlelit welcome dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light welcome bites and tropical fruit platter served upon arrival at the villa
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the resort's signature overwater fine-dining restaurant — a curated 4-course set menu featuring fresh Maldivian lobster, grilled reef fish, and a bottle of champagne compliments of the resort

day_by_day.notes: Request early luggage delivery to villa so you can freshen up quickly after the boat transfer. Confirm any dietary preferences with the resort concierge upon arrival. The resort may offer a honeymoon welcome package — ensure this is pre-arranged before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with a private in-villa breakfast served on your overwater deck as the morning light sparkles across the lagoon. After breakfast, gear up for the Private Lagoon Snorkeling at the House Reef — snorkel directly from your overwater bungalow steps into the resort's pristine house reef. A dedicated marine biologist guide will accompany you to point out vibrant coral gardens, sea turtles, reef sharks, and tropical fish. Session lasts approximately 90 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the villa for a refreshing outdoor rain shower and a light poolside lunch. Spend the afternoon at leisure — lounge on your private sun deck, dip into your plunge pool, or book a couples' session at the resort spa featuring traditional Maldivian Boduberu healing massage techniques.
day_by_day.evening: As dusk approaches, board a private dhoni for the Sunset Dolphin Cruise for Two. Watch spinner dolphins leap alongside the boat as the sky turns shades of gold and pink. Sip on chilled prosecco and canapés while your captain navigates the calm Indian Ocean waters. Return to the resort for a romantic beachside dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Private in-villa breakfast on the overwater deck — tropical fruit selection, freshly baked pastries, eggs cooked to order, Maldivian short eats, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside light lunch at the resort's beach club — grilled prawn skewers, fresh salads, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Romantic beachside dinner on the private sandbank setup — grilled catch of the day, saffron risotto, and a shared dessert platter with sparkling wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sunset Dolphin Cruise in advance through the concierge — best departure time is around 17:30 to align with sunset. Apply reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. The house reef is best explored during mid-morning when visibility is at its peak.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a peaceful yoga session on the overwater yoga pavilion at sunrise — arrange this with the resort's wellness team the evening before. Breathe in the ocean air as the sun rises over the atoll. Follow with a hearty in-villa breakfast. Spend the late morning exploring the resort island on foot or by bicycle, discovering hidden beach coves and lush tropical gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a 2-hour luxury couples' spa treatment at the resort's overwater spa. Choose from signature Maldivian rituals using locally sourced ingredients such as coconut oil, sea salt, and tropical flowers. After the spa, cool off with a swim in the resort's infinity pool overlooking the ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Dress up for a truly unforgettable Underwater Restaurant Dining Experience. Descend into the resort's or a nearby world-renowned underwater restaurant where coral reefs and marine life surround you through floor-to-ceiling glass panels. Enjoy a curated 5-course tasting menu with wine pairings as manta rays and reef fish glide past your table.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast — acai bowls, smoked salmon bagels, fresh juices, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Light post-spa refreshments at the spa lounge — herbal teas, fresh fruit platters, and raw energy bites
meals.dinner: Underwater Restaurant — 5-course fine-dining tasting menu with premium wine pairing; expect dishes like tuna tartare, lobster bisque, Wagyu beef, and a decadent chocolate fondant dessert

day_by_day.notes: The Underwater Restaurant requires advance reservation — book at least 2–3 days ahead as it is extremely popular. Dress code is smart casual. Confirm the specific underwater restaurant available from North Malé Atoll with your concierge, as Ithaa at Conrad Maldives is a nearby iconic option accessible by speedboat.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed morning with breakfast in bed — arrange a special honeymoon breakfast tray with the concierge the night before. After breakfast, take a guided snorkeling session at a nearby reef patch accessible by the resort's house boat. Focus on spotting sea turtles and eagle rays in the shallow lagoon waters of North Malé Atoll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a private speedboat excursion to explore the surrounding uninhabited sandbanks of North Malé Atoll. Anchor at a secluded white sandbank and enjoy a private picnic lunch set up by the resort — complete with chilled wine, artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and a beach umbrella. Swim and snorkel in the crystal-clear shallows around the sandbank.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a quiet evening. Watch the sunset from your private villa deck with a bottle of champagne. Dine at the resort's main restaurant for a relaxed à la carte dinner featuring Maldivian and international fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Honeymoon breakfast in bed — heart-shaped pancakes, fresh berries, mimosas, eggs benedict, and tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Private sandbank picnic — gourmet sandwiches, charcuterie board, tropical fruits, macarons, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: À la carte dinner at the resort's main restaurant — grilled barramundi, coconut curry, and mango panna cotta for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Coordinate the private sandbank picnic with the concierge at least one day in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a hat for the sandbank excursion as shade is minimal. This is an ideal day for photography — bring a waterproof camera.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with an early morning stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) session on the calm lagoon — the water is glassiest before 9:00 AM. Enjoy the meditative experience of paddling across the turquoise waters with views of the overwater bungalows. Return for a leisurely breakfast at the resort's open-air beach restaurant.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a speedboat transfer to the local inhabited island of Maafushi for the Maldivian Cultural Village Tour. Explore traditional Maldivian architecture, visit a local school or mosque (respectfully), watch artisans weave traditional 'thundu kunaa' mats, and sample local street food and short eats. Learn about the history and culture of the Maldives from a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a private romantic dinner on the beach — arranged by the resort with a dedicated butler, tiki torches, flower petal decorations, and a bespoke menu. Perfect for a special honeymoon evening.

meals.breakfast: Beach restaurant breakfast — Maldivian mas huni (tuna and coconut salad) with roshi flatbread, fresh juices, and coffee
meals.lunch: Local food tasting on Maafushi Island — sample traditional Maldivian short eats including bajiyaa (fish pastries), gulha (fish balls), and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Private romantic beach dinner — 4-course bespoke menu featuring lobster thermidor, champagne risotto, and a custom honeymoon dessert with a personalized message

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for the Maafushi cultural tour — cover shoulders and knees as a sign of respect on the local island. The tour typically takes 2–3 hours. Arrange the private beach dinner with your butler at least 48 hours in advance for the best setup.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a full relaxation day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast on your villa deck. Book a private cooking class with the resort's executive chef to learn how to prepare traditional Maldivian dishes — mas riha (fish curry), coconut sambol, and banana leaf desserts.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class, enjoy the dishes you prepared for a private lunch in the resort's garden. Spend the afternoon at the resort's overwater infinity pool with a cocktail in hand. Try the resort's signature cocktail menu and enjoy the afternoon sun.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the resort's rooftop or elevated deck for stargazing — request a private stargazing session with a telescope through the concierge. Many Maldivian resorts offer guided astronomy experiences. Afterward, enjoy a light dinner at the resort's tapas and cocktail bar.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely in-villa deck breakfast — granola, yogurt, tropical fruits, avocado toast, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Private garden lunch featuring dishes prepared during your cooking class — Maldivian fish curry, coconut rice, and fresh salad
meals.dinner: Tapas and cocktail bar dinner — sharing plates of tuna tataki, truffle arancini, seared scallops, and artisan cheese board with craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a wonderful honeymoon memory — ask the resort to photograph the session for you. Stargazing is best on clear nights away from light pollution; North Malé Atoll offers excellent visibility. Confirm stargazing availability with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a morning big game fishing excursion — arrange a private chartered fishing boat through the resort. Try your hand at catch-and-release sport fishing in the deep waters of the Indian Ocean. The experienced captain will guide you to the best fishing spots. Species commonly found include yellowfin tuna, wahoo, and dorado.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from fishing by early afternoon. If you caught any fish, the resort's chef can prepare it for you as a personalized lunch — a truly farm-to-table (or ocean-to-table) experience. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach with a good book and refreshing drinks from the beach bar.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a couples' sunset cocktail hour at the resort's overwater bar. As night falls, dine at the resort's specialty Japanese-inspired Teppanyaki or sushi restaurant (if available at the property) for a fun, interactive dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before fishing — continental spread with pastries, fruit, yogurt, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Ocean-to-table lunch — your freshly caught fish grilled with herbs and lemon butter, served with roasted vegetables and saffron rice
meals.dinner: Specialty restaurant dinner — premium sashimi platter, wagyu beef teppanyaki, miso soup, and matcha dessert with sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the fishing charter at least 2 days in advance. Bring motion sickness medication if needed as the open ocean can have some swell. The ocean-to-table lunch concept should be pre-arranged with the chef so they are ready to prepare your catch upon return.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full-day excursion to Hanifaru Bay in Baa Atoll for the legendary Manta Ray Snorkeling experience — one of the most extraordinary wildlife encounters in the world. Depart early by speedboat (approximately 1.5–2 hours depending on location). Upon arrival at the UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, snorkel alongside dozens of majestic manta rays feeding in the nutrient-rich waters. A certified marine guide accompanies you throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling at Hanifaru Bay or nearby reef sites in Baa Atoll. Enjoy a packed gourmet lunch provided by the resort on the boat — dine on the water surrounded by the stunning atoll scenery. Explore additional snorkeling spots in the area before beginning the return journey.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the resort by late afternoon. Rest and rejuvenate with an in-villa couple's massage arranged through the spa. Enjoy a quiet, intimate dinner at the resort's main restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-excursion breakfast at the resort — energy-boosting spread of eggs, whole grain toast, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed boat lunch — artisan wraps, fresh salads, tropical fruit, energy bars, and chilled beverages on the boat
meals.dinner: Resort main restaurant — pan-seared sea bass, truffle pasta, and a shared chocolate lava cake with vanilla ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Manta ray sightings at Hanifaru Bay are most prolific between May and November, but March can still offer encounters. Confirm seasonal availability with the concierge. This excursion requires early departure — set an alarm. Only reef-safe sunscreen is permitted in the UNESCO reserve. No touching or chasing of marine life.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a well-deserved rest morning after yesterday's full-day excursion. Sleep in and have a leisurely in-villa breakfast. Spend the late morning at the resort's private beach — build sandcastles, collect shells, or simply lie in the sun listening to the gentle waves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Book an afternoon session of water sports at the resort's water sports center — try jet skiing, parasailing, or a fun tube ride across the lagoon. Alternatively, opt for a more serene kayaking session through the mangroves or around the island's perimeter.
day_by_day.evening: As the sun sets, enjoy a second Sunset Dolphin Cruise for Two if you wish to relive the magic — or opt for a private overwater dinner setup at the end of the jetty. The resort can arrange a table on the jetty with lanterns, flower petals, and a personalized menu.

meals.breakfast: In-villa slow breakfast — smoked salmon eggs royale, fresh pastries, fruit platter, and freshly brewed specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch — lobster rolls, crispy calamari, fresh guacamole with nachos, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Overwater jetty private dinner — 4-course romantic menu with champagne, grilled langoustines, beef tenderloin, and a strawberry soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Water sports availability depends on weather and sea conditions — confirm with the water sports center in the morning. The overwater jetty dinner is one of the most romantic experiences available; book it through the concierge at least 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the morning with a guided snorkeling session at a different reef site accessible from the resort — focus on discovering new marine life not seen at the house reef. The resort's marine biologist can suggest the best nearby spots. After snorkeling, enjoy a refreshing swim and morning tea on your villa deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort's overwater spa for an extended wellness ritual. Book the 'Maldivian Journey' package — a 3-hour treatment combining a coconut milk body scrub, hot stone massage, and a nourishing hair and scalp treatment. Emerge feeling completely revitalized.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the midpoint of your honeymoon with a special evening. Ask the concierge to arrange a private movie night on the beach — a projector screen set up on the sand with bean bags, blankets, popcorn, and a selection of your favorite films under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Beach restaurant breakfast — Maldivian breakfast spread with mas huni, roshi, fresh fruits, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Post-spa light lunch at the spa lounge — detox green smoothies, grain bowls, and fresh tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Beachside movie night dinner — gourmet picnic boxes with sliders, truffle fries, artisan popcorn flavors, and a dessert board with s'mores kit

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the beach movie night experience with the concierge at least 48 hours in advance. Choose your film preferences and any special snacks or beverages. This is a wonderfully unique and intimate honeymoon experience that most luxury resorts in the Maldives can accommodate.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning on a private guided boat tour to explore the surrounding atolls and islands of North Malé. Visit uninhabited islands, search for sea turtles nesting on beaches, and snorkel at a pristine coral garden. The private boat ensures a completely exclusive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by early afternoon. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the resort's infinity pool with cocktails. Treat yourselves to an ice cream and fresh juice break at the resort's beach kiosk. Take some time to shop at the resort boutique for Maldivian souvenirs and keepsakes.
day_by_day.evening: Dress elegantly for a Chef's Table experience — an exclusive private dining event where the resort's executive chef personally prepares and presents a bespoke multi-course meal at a dedicated private table, explaining each dish and its inspiration.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast — avocado toast, poached eggs, smoked salmon, fresh juices, and a selection of teas
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch — grilled fish tacos, mango salsa, fresh lime margaritas, and tropical fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Chef's Table — 7-course bespoke tasting menu with wine pairing; dishes inspired by the ocean and Maldivian ingredients, presented personally by the executive chef

day_by_day.notes: The Chef's Table is one of the most exclusive dining experiences available — reserve it as early as possible, ideally before arrival. Dress code is smart elegant. This experience typically accommodates only one or two couples per evening.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the penultimate morning to a final snorkeling adventure — revisit your favorite reef spots and take underwater photographs to capture memories of the incredible marine life you've encountered throughout the trip. Many resorts offer underwater photography sessions with a professional photographer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon indulging in a final couples' spa session — choose a relaxing treatment to unwind. Afterward, pack any items you won't need for the final day and organize your belongings. Take a slow walk around the island one last time, pausing at your favorite spots.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your final full evening in the Maldives with a grand farewell dinner. Request the resort's most special setup — a private overwater platform or sandbank dinner with elaborate floral decorations, a live musician (guitarist or violinist), and a premium menu featuring the finest ingredients available.

meals.breakfast: Final morning splurge breakfast — full à la carte in-villa breakfast with champagne, eggs any style, smoked salmon, pastries, and tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Beach bar farewell lunch — grilled reef fish, coconut rice, fresh salad, and a celebratory dessert
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner — private overwater setup with live music, 5-course premium menu featuring caviar, lobster, and a personalized honeymoon cake

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the farewell dinner well in advance and communicate any special requests (honeymoon cake message, flower preferences, music style). Consider purchasing a memory book or photo album from the resort's photography service to commemorate your trip. Tip your butler and service staff generously as a gesture of appreciation.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise on your private villa deck — a quiet, reflective moment to absorb the beauty of the Maldives one last time. Enjoy a final in-villa breakfast as you watch the morning light dance on the lagoon. Take a last dip in your plunge pool and soak in every last moment of paradise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort with assistance from your dedicated butler who will handle all luggage. Receive a warm farewell from the resort team with parting gifts. Board the private luxury speedboat transfer back to Velana International Airport. Arrive at the airport with ample time for departure formalities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Velana International Airport. Carry with you unforgettable memories, photographs, and the joy of an extraordinary honeymoon in the Maldives.
